findings.title: Unbounded ship_judgment evidence can push the Epic page JSON past its hard 1.5MB budget and permanently stop refreshes
findings.detail: readEpicJudgment embeds the raw parsed evaluation (`result_json`, DB CHECK allows up to 65536 bytes) and the raw `mechanical_json` (bounded only by the ~98304-byte opinion-candidate budget in opinions.ts, plus the serialized binding) into `EpicJudgment.evidence`, and generate.ts:209 attaches that whole value as a per-item Cell on the Epic page. The HTML path was deliberately bounded (render-html.ts renderJudgment keeps only a summary + sidecar link, and optional-budget.ts binary-searches `judgmentRows`/`historyRows`), but the JSON document has no equivalent reduction: applyAttentionBudget (attention-budget.ts:104) can only drop `attention` entries, and materialize.ts:149 then calls assertEpicPage, which throws EpicPageSchemaError once canonicalJsonString(page) exceeds EPIC_PAGE_MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES (model.ts:20, 1507328). I verified this empirically against the project's own stress fixture pageForShipJudgmentBudget(60): with `evidence.evaluation = null` the document is 997334 bytes, leaving only ~510KB of headroom for all judgment evidence combined; injecting 30 items x 20KB of evaluation JSON yields 1571024 bytes and assertEpicPage throws `document exceeds 1507328 bytes`. runEpicPageAttempt (epic-page-refresher.ts:113-118) catches it and settles the attempt as unavailable, so the Bridge survives but the flywheel Epic page silently stops materializing/publishing on every subsequent attempt with no self-healing path, since nothing trims ship_judgment. Note the budget fixture added in this change uses `evidence: { evaluation: null, mechanical: null }` (fixtures/founder-budget.ts:128), so the existing budget tests never exercise the realistic payload.
findings.failure_scenario: flywheel auto-narrow flag is set to dry_run; over a few days ~15-30 active Epic items accumulate opinions whose `result_json` is 20-64KB (100 requirements / 200 use cases with 500-codepoint quotes, as the prompt permits) plus `mechanical_json` with hundreds of overlap entries. The next epic-page refresh builds a document whose canonical JSON exceeds 1507328 bytes; assertEpicPage throws, runEpicPageAttempt records `structural`/`unavailable`, and the founder's Epic page is frozen at its last good version indefinitely.

findings.title: modeSweep accepts `off` and can PATCH Discord after the kill switch is flipped
findings.detail: runtime.ts:85 short-circuits `off` with the comment "off must never run a transport sweep", and the unit test "off closes existing opinion accounting as history without observation or transport" asserts modeSweep is never invoked in off. But the bridge modeSweep re-reads `deps.mode()` and explicitly allows "off" (`if (mode !== "dry_run" && mode !== "auto" && mode !== "off") return;`), and it is reached only after `await this.deps.learningSweep(...)` which performs up to two Discord requests with 10s timeouts. Flipping the flag to off inside that window leaves `enabled: () => deps.mode() === mode` true for mode === "off", and claimHistory only rejects `delivery_mode === 'dry_run'`, so the sweep still issues up to two history PATCH/scan calls to Discord after the kill switch was thrown. Restricting modeSweep's allowed set to dry_run/auto (or re-checking for off before the history loop) closes it.
findings.failure_scenario: Founder flips the flywheel auto-narrow flag from dry_run to off while a modeTick is blocked in learningSweep awaiting Discord. modeSweep then runs with mode === "off", calls setMode("off") and proceeds into the historyWork loop, editing up to two of the bot's opinion messages in the founder's thread after the feature was supposed to be fully stopped.

findings.title: Startup freeze invalidation creates rows that listAutoNarrowOpinionDeliveryWork returns forever but beginAutoNarrowOpinionDelivery always refuses
findings.detail: invalidateAutoNarrowLegacyFreezeOnStartup runs unconditionally on every Bridge boot (plugin.ts:11940), regardless of mode, and sets `legacy_frozen_at=NULL, legacy_freeze_requested_at=COALESCE(...), next_attempt_at=NULL` on every previously-frozen row. requestAutoNarrowLegacyFreeze marks rows with `followup_message_id IS NULL AND state NOT IN ('posting','uncertain')` as frozen without ever sending anything, so those rows keep `state='pending'`. After a restart in auto or off mode such a row is selected by listAutoNarrowOpinionDeliveryWork (StateStore.ts:54425 — `legacy_frozen_at IS NULL`, state<>'delivered', next_attempt_at NULL so it sorts first under `ORDER BY COALESCE(next_attempt_at,'')`), but beginAutoNarrowOpinionDelivery (StateStore.ts:54451) refuses because `current.legacyFreezeRequestedAt` is set, and the reconcile loop's `if (!claimed) { result.skipped += 1; continue; }` writes no backoff and no state change. The only clearer is ensureAutoNarrowLegacyIntentTx, which runs solely from refreshAutoNarrowOpinionsIfEligible during card materialization (never for already-completed holders, and never at all in off mode, which returns `{status:'off'}` first). The rows therefore occupy the head of the fixed 20-row sweep window permanently with no recovery path.
findings.failure_scenario: flywheel runs in dry_run long enough for the legacy freeze to mark N undelivered pending deliveries (followup_message_id NULL) as frozen; the founder rolls the flag back to auto (or off) and the Bridge restarts (launchd restarts are routine). Those N rows reappear un-frozen with next_attempt_at NULL, sort first, and are skipped on every sweep forever, cutting the legacy auto-narrow opinion/label sweep budget from 20 to 20-N per tick — total starvation once N reaches 20.

findings.title: Evaluator subprocess switched from `--setting-sources ""` to `user`, widening its config surface
findings.detail: The rework changed the isolated evaluator from an empty setting-sources list to `user` so subscription identity resolves (rework.md F2). Tools, MCP, plugins and hooks are still explicitly disabled and `--model`/`--system-prompt` are pinned on argv, so the main risks are covered, but `~/.claude/settings.json` can still contribute non-hook executable config (e.g. `apiKeyHelper`, `env`, `permissions`) to a process whose whole point is deterministic, reproducible replay. Worth a comment at the flag and a note in the replay report so a future reader does not assume the child is config-isolated.
findings.failure_scenario: A developer adds `apiKeyHelper` or `env` entries to their user settings; the ship-judgment evaluator subprocess silently picks them up, so a replay of the same frozen packet on two machines is no longer guaranteed to be equivalent, and `scripts/replay-ship-judgment.mjs` output is not reproducible across hosts.

findings.title: Issue source hard-requires an FLY- identifier, so GEO- Flywheel runs can never produce an opinion
findings.detail: issueSchema pins `identifier` to `/^FLY-[1-9][0-9]*$/` and readJudgmentIssueSource returns null for anything else, which collect.ts turns into `issue_missing` → permanently undetermined. The project's CLAUDE.md states that historical Flywheel issues stay under the GEO- prefix and are not migrated, and workflow_run.issue_id for those runs is the GEO- identifier. Such cards will silently sit at "不可判定" with reason `issue_missing` forever rather than reporting a scope mismatch. Accepting `(FLY|GEO)-\d+` (or at least emitting a distinguishable reason code) would avoid a confusing permanent-undetermined state.
findings.failure_scenario: A flywheel-project run whose Linear issue is GEO-1234 reaches a ship card in dry_run; every scan collects sources, readJudgmentIssueSource returns null, and the card's machine opinion is always "不可判定 · issue_missing" with no signal that the cause is the identifier prefix rather than a missing issue.
